items.title: Why cracking your knuckles doesn't cause arthritis
items.summary: Does cracking your knuckles cause arthritis? Dr. Donald Unger cracked only his left hand's knuckles for more than 60 years and kept the right as a control. Neither hand developed arthritis, and he won the 2009 Ig Nobel Prize in Medicine. In 2015, researchers filmed a knuckle crack in a real-time MRI and saw the crack come as a cavity formed in the joint. Sources: Ig Nobel Prize 2009 (Improbable Research); Kawchuk GN et al., "Real-Time Visualization of Joint Cavitation", PLOS ONE 10(4), 2015. Idea: AsapSCIENCE. Which knuckle do you crack first? #Shorts #health #science

items.title: Why you can't fold paper more than 7 times
items.summary: Why you can't fold paper more than 7 times. Seven folds is already 128 layers. In January 2002, high school junior Britney Gallivan folded a roll of toilet paper about 4,000 feet long 12 times. At 42 folds, 0.1 mm paper would be 439,805 km tall, past the Moon at 384,400 km. Sources: Guinness World Records (most times to fold a piece of paper), MathWorld "Folding", NASA Moon Fact Sheet. Idea: Hafu Go. Fold one yourself: how far do you get? #Shorts #math #science

items.title: Why a coin flip isn't 50/50
items.summary: A coin flip isn't 50/50. Researchers flipped coins 350,757 times. Heads and tails came out even at 0.500. But the side that started facing up landed up 50.8% of the time. A flipped coin wobbles, so it spends a little more time with the starting side up. A 2007 physics model by Diaconis, Holmes and Montgomery predicted about 51%. The 2023 data landed on 50.8%.Why a coin flip isn't 50/50. Researchers flipped coins 350,757 times. Heads and tails came out even, but the side that started facing up landed up 50.8% of the time, because a flipped coin wobbles. Source: Bartos et al. 2023, "Fair coins tend to land on the same side they started" (arXiv 2310.04153). Prediction: Diaconis, Holmes and Montgomery 2007. Idea: Mark Rober. Call it before you flip: same side or the other? #Shorts #coinflip #probability Idea: Mark Rober. Sources: Bartos et al. 2023, "Fair coins tend to land on the same side they started" (arXiv 2310.04153). Diaconis, Holmes and Montgomery 2007. Call it before you flip: same side or the other?

items.title: Vì sao người Việt có cái nhìn tích cực về AI?
items.summary: [English below] Khảo sát từ Gallup cho thấy phần lớn người Việt có thái độ cởi mở với AI, đồng thời chỉ hơn 20% lo ngại nguy cơ mất việc - một tỷ lệ tương đối thấp so với mặt bằng chung thế giới. Nhìn từ cơ cấu thị trường, ông Ralf Matthaes đã có những lý giải nhất định về tâm lý này. Xem phiên bản đầy đủ tập 417 Vietnam Innovators (Tiếng Anh) trên các kênh Youtube, Spotify & Apple Podcasts của Vietnam Innovators Digest để lắng nghe trọn vẹn chia sẻ từ ông Ralf Matthaes - Founder & Managing Director, Infocus Mekong Research (IFM Research). - A Gallup survey shows that the majority of Vietnamese hold an open attitude toward AI, while just over 20% express concern about losing their jobs, a relatively low rate compared to the global average. Looking from the perspective of market structure, Mr. Ralf Matthaes - Founder & Managing Director, Infocus Mekong Research (IFM Research), offers notable context behind this sentiment. Listen more from EP 417 of Vietnam Innovators (English Edition), available on Vietnam Innovators Digest’s YouTube, Spotify, and Apple Podcasts.
